question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Under the Hornbostel-Sachs framework, musical instruments are grouped according to the way they generate sound. Take the darbuka, an instrument widely played in Lebanon, which produces its sound chiefly from the vibrations of a taut membrane. ______ within the Hornbostel-Sachs system, the darbuka counts as a membranophone.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The classification follows as a conclusion from how the darbuka makes sound, so 'Thus' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Los Angeles paid tribute to the editor and socialite Ethel Shorb by naming Ethel Avenue ______ her.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between 'after' and its object 'her.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Naomi Iizuka wrote the 2002 play 36 Views. ______ play had its first performance at the Berkeley Repertory Theatre in California.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A singular demonstrative determiner is needed before 'play,' so 'This' is correct.

question: Which quotation from Cane most effectively illustrates the claim? Cane is a 1923 novel by Jean Toomer. In it, Toomer refers to a rural Georgia road named Dixie Pike and portrays it as deeply tied to a distant land, writing, ______
option a: "And when the wind is from the South, soil of my homeland falls like a fertile shower upon the lean streets of [Washington, DC]."
option b: "From down the railroad track, the chug-chug of a gas engine announces that the repair gang is coming home."
option c: "Dixie Pike is what they call it."
option d: "The Dixie Pike has grown from a goat path in Africa."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Tracing the road's origin to Africa shows its connection to a faraway place.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?

Highly Traveled Commercial Airline Routes in 2017-18
Location 1 | Location 2 | Distance of route (kilometers) | 2018 passengers | 2017 passengers | Domestic or international
Hong Kong | Manila | 1,145 | 3,008,842 | 2,907,228 | international
Jakarta | Singapore | 896 | 4,812,342 | 4,810,602 | international
Mumbai | Delhi | 1,150 | 7,392,155 | 7,129,943 | domestic
Mexico City | Monterrey | 729 | 3,474,971 | 3,202,091 | domestic

An examination of the busiest commercial airline routes for 2017 and 2018 found that, as a rule, domestic routes (those staying within a single country) transported far more passengers than international ones. Even so, a handful of international routes proved popular enough to move more travelers than several of the most heavily used domestic routes, as becomes clear when one compares the ______
option a: distance between Mexico City and Monterrey with the distance between Jakarta and Singapore.
option b: number of passengers who traveled between Mumbai and Delhi in 2017 with the number who traveled between Hong Kong and Manila during that same year.
option c: number of passengers who traveled between Jakarta and Singapore in 2017 with the number who traveled that same route in 2018.
option d: number of passengers who traveled between Jakarta and Singapore in 2018 with the number who traveled between Mexico City and Monterrey during that same year.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The international Jakarta-Singapore route carried more 2018 passengers than the domestic Mexico City-Monterrey route.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Norway's constitution, adopted in 1814 and running to 7,307 words, unlike Ireland's, which was adopted in 1937 and holds a much larger count of 16,007 words, ______ as the 21st shortest in the world. Figures like these are examined by constitutional scholars such as Dominic J. Nardi, who can draw broader conclusions from them.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'constitution' requires the singular present-tense verb 'ranks.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Los Angeles honored the professor Dr. Jane Bancroft Robinson by naming Robinson Road ______ her.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation should separate 'after' from its object 'her.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Talk-Story, written by Jeannie Barroga in 1992, is a play. ______ play was first staged at TheatreWorks in California.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A singular demonstrative determiner is needed before 'play,' so 'This' is correct.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? A great many of the writings of the Greek astronomer Hipparchus (2nd century BCE) are ______ his Commentary, a critique of a well-known astronomical poem, is an extant work: it can still be read.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Two independent clauses require a period, and the contrast word 'Conversely' is set off by a comma.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Alicia Pérez-Porro works as a biologist at the Smithsonian ______ conducts research on sea sponges.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period plus the subject pronoun 'She' correctly separates two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The Doric Hexapolis, an alliance of six coastal cities across Greece and Turkey that peaked around 1000 BCE, is regarded as a thalassocracy--a political power whose dominance came from mastery of the sea rather than the land. Historians treat thalassocracies as separate from tellurocracies, or land-based powers. ______ the Spanish Empire (1500s-1900s CE) is recognized for supremacy on both land and sea.
option a: In other words, empires are classified according to their source of power:
option b: Of course, the distinction is not always so neat:
option c: For example, tellurocracies have long overpowered their rivals:
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The Spanish Empire's dual supremacy shows the two categories are not always cleanly separate.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The 1904 novel Cabbages and Kings, written by William Sydney Porter, did not carry Porter's own name on its cover. That is because Porter decided ______ a pen name: O. Henry.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The verb 'decided' takes the infinitive 'to use.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Boo and His Rabbit is a photograph by the British artist Chris Killip. Killip made ______ in 1984.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular pronoun 'it' refers to the single photograph.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? A widely read literary magazine of the Victorian age, ______ whose novel The Caxtons appeared there across fourteen installments from April 1848 to October 1849.
option a: Blackwood's Magazine published serialized versions of novels by Edward Bulwer-Lytton and other prominent writers of the day,
option b: serialized versions of novels by prominent writers of the day, including Edward Bulwer-Lytton, were published in Blackwood's Magazine,
option c: Blackwood's Magazine published serialized versions of novels by prominent writers of the day, including Edward Bulwer-Lytton,
option d: prominent writers of the day published serialized versions of their novels in Blackwood's Magazine, including Edward Bulwer-Lytton,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The opening modifier must attach to 'Blackwood's Magazine,' and the 'whose' clause must follow the named writer, Edward Bulwer-Lytton.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In Vietnam, a Southeast Asian nation, the share of the population living in cities grew from 33.8% to 37.3% between 2015 and 2020. ______ urbanization rates rose across Southeast Asia as a whole, climbing 2.8 percentage points over that five-year period.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both trends happen over the same 2015-2020 span, so 'Concurrently' fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Researchers in France assert that leopards and brown bears rank among the twenty most "charismatic" animals (that is, "attractive, fascinating, or appealing"). To assemble this top-twenty list, the researchers relied on survey data gathered in Western Europe. The way Europeans regard leopards and brown bears might not be shared elsewhere in the world, ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Of course' acknowledges the natural limitation of a Europe-based survey.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Although today's composers often draw inspiration from earlier masters such as Johann Sebastian Bach, the range of what shapes them is wide. Gabriela Montero's music, for instance, can be said to ______ features of both the classical European tradition and the social, political, and cultural landscape of her native Venezuela.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Her music displays, or 'exhibits,' features of both traditions.

question: Which quotation from a publication by a researcher would most effectively support the student's claim? A student is writing an essay about cultured meat, which is grown in a laboratory and is meant to help lower the number of livestock slaughtered for food. The student wants to argue that producing cultured meat may be helpful in responding to an anticipated widespread shift in the public's behavior.
option a: "Consumers tend to believe that using less packaging when selling meat products in stores would have a significant effect on the environment."
option b: "A growing population that is including significantly more meat in its diet will contribute to an increasing demand for meat products in the 21st century."
option c: "Researchers who advocate for the development of lab-grown meat claim that it's better than conventional meat because its nutritional content can be adjusted."
option d: "Some of the growth promoters that would be needed to produce large quantities of cultured meats are currently prohibited for farming purposes in the European Union."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A population eating more meat is the expected behavior change that cultured meat could help meet.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? June is the First Fall, written by Yilong Liu in 2018, is a play. ______ play was first performed at the Kumu Kahua Theatre in Honolulu.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A singular demonstrative determiner is needed before 'play,' so 'This' is correct.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The novel Animal Farm, published by Eric Arthur Blair in 1945, did not display Blair's real name on its cover. That is because Blair opted ______ a pen name: George Orwell.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The verb 'opted' takes the infinitive 'to use.'
